question.explanation:
Note that all of the terms have a common factor of $n^3.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $n^3,$ as follows:

\begin{align} 3 n^5 + 17 n^4 - 28 n^3& = n^3(3n^2 + 17n - 28) \end{align}

Now, we factor the polynomial $3n^2 + 17n - 28,$ as follows: \begin{align} n^3(3n^2 + 17n - 28) & = \\[3pt] n^3((3n^2-4n) + (21n-28)) & = \\[3pt] n^3((3n-4)n +(3n-4)7) & = \\[3pt] n^3(3n-4)(n+7) \end{align}

example.title: Factoring Using Common Factors and Quadratic Factoring

question.explanation:
First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $s^4.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $s^4,$ as follows:

\begin{align} s^6 - 4s^5 + 4s^4 & = s^4(s^2 - 4s + 4) \end{align}

The expression $s^2 - 4s + 4$ is a perfect square trinomial that can be factored as follows: \begin{align} s^4(s^2 - 4s + 4) & = \\[3pt] s^4(s^2 -4s + 2^2) & = \\[3pt] s^4(s^2 - 2 \cdot 2\cdot s + 2^2) & = \\[3pt] s^4(s -2)^2 \end{align}

example.title: Factoring Using Common Factors and Perfect Square Trinomials

question.explanation:
First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $h^5.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $h^5,$ as follows:

\begin{align} h^7 + 8 h^6 + 16 h^5 & = h^5(h^2 + 8h + 16) \end{align}

The expression $h^2 + 8h + 16$ is a perfect square trinomial that can be factored as follows: \begin{align} h^5(h^2 + 8h + 16) & = \\[3pt] h^5(h^2 + 8h + 4^2) & = \\[3pt] h^5(h^2 + 2 \cdot 4h + 4^2) & = \\[3pt] h^5(h + 4)^2 \end{align}
